result.title: Instead of asking why they stay, ask how we can help #TEDTalks
result.description: Leslie Morgan Steiner was in "crazy love" -- that is, madly in love with a man who routinely abused her and threatened her life. Steiner tells the story of her relationship, correcting misconceptions many people hold about victims of domestic violence, and explaining how we can all help break the silence.

result.title: The Art of Disagreeing with Dignity | Tami Pyfer | TED
result.description:
Tami Pyfer has five kids who belong to five different political parties, and sometimes family conversations get heated. Drawing on her work as a former policy advisor to the governor of Utah, she wanted to find a healthier way for people to talk about politics without contempt. The result is the Dignity Index: an eight-point scale that measures the language we use to disagree, aiming to ease political divisions. What score do you think your last conversation would get? (Recorded at TED Democracy Philadelphia on June 13, 2026)

result.title: How to Make Parenting Less Lonely | Stacey McLachlan | TED
result.description:
When parents first have kids, some risk entering “the loneliest decade,” where they fall out of touch with friends. Writer Stacey McLachlan decided to do something different when she had her daughter, refusing to let her social life slip away. In this witty talk, she shares her solution — and why it matters for all of us. (Recorded at TEDxVancouver on March 8, 2026)

result.title: Are Your Dealbreakers Sabotaging Your Love Life? | Amy Chan | TED
result.description:
Relationship expert Amy Chan believes we’re in a "relationship recession,” fueled by modern daters constantly looking for what could go wrong. But what if your dealbreakers are the very thing keeping love out? In this relatable talk, she reveals how to discover true connection — and why the right person for you might not be who you expect.

result.title: Authoritarianism isn’t winning, democracy is failing, says Sally Kohn #TEDTalks
result.description: Doesn't it seem like a lot of online news sites have moved beyond reporting the news to openly inciting your outrage (and your page views)? News analyst Sally Kohn suggests — don't engage with news that looks like it just wants to make you mad. Instead, give your precious clicks to the news sites you truly trust.
